text:
ashley: starting a focused spike: reduce long-lived CP <-> tenant VPC tunnels. aim: smaller handshake surface, explicit fallback semantics, safer DNS behavior. posting scope and quick plan.

oliver: summary? are we replacing peering for new tenants or adding a different default?

ashley: not forcing change. default-new = ephemeral handshake (short mTLS session created on demand), then prefer agentless private endpoint. peering/persistent-relay remain supported by policy.

tess: how are we doing auth for ephemeral sessions? CSR-based certs, tokens, or pre-provisioned creds?

ashley: CSR flow + KMS signer. tenant agent submits CSR over authenticated channel, we return short-lived cert (1-15m for bootstrap). agent-managed certs can be longer and auto-renewed. tokens only for fallback relays and with revocation hooks.

kevin: need concrete SLOs/SLIs to gate rollout: TLS handshake median p95, fallback-rate, cert-issuance latency, and control-plane CPU-per-handshake. propose fallback-rate alert at 0.3% over 10m.

sam: ops note: ensure an easy per-tenant kill switch to re-enable persistent-relay and a bulk view to find tenants currently in ephemeral mode.

oliver: DNS concerns? ephemeral endpoints can lead to cache issues and resolver TTLs.

ashley: agree. plan DNS pattern: ephemeral subdomain with 3s TTL for first 2 minutes post-onboard, then 30s TTL once stable. SDKs should honor TTL and provide forced refresh hooks. also publish resolver guidance for on-prem proxies.

tess: how to avoid handshake storms at scale? if thousands of agents restart, CP could get hammered.

ashley: mitigation: regional backoff windows with jitter, per-region leader that batches cert renewals, and small in-line token-caching window (reuse cert for N requests). we'll also rate-limit cert signing requests on KMS.

kevin: we should capture NAT/backing behavior: number of ephemeral connections per-source, SYN reset rate, and observed client-source-port reuse. add a NAT-flap test.

sam: rollout steps suggestion: alpha internal only; beta opt-in customers; canary 0.5% production traffic; ramp with automatic rollback if fallback-rate > 0.3% or TLS p95 > 200ms.

oliver: sample policy we can surface to devs?

ashley: quick example (discussion-friendly):

```
handshake:
  strategy: ephemeral-csr
  bootstrap_ttl: 900   # seconds
  reuse_for_requests: 5
  batch_renew_jitter_ms: 30000
cert:
  issuer: redwood-kms
  ttl_seconds: 900
fallback:
  relay_enable: true
  relay_grace_period: 600
  fallback_triggers:
    - name: tls_failures
      threshold: 5
      window_seconds: 300
```

kevin: add runtime flag to force-relay per-tenant for debugging. also log a compact audit trail for every certificate issuance (who/when/reason).

tess: security review pointers: bind cert SANs to tenant ID and allowed IP ranges, audit CSR origin, HSM-backed signing, and make revocation observable.

sam: automation: canary-bot should run periodic churn tests during canary and create PRs to the dashboard if metrics deviate. also we need a runbook to enable per-tenant rollback and a synthetic probe that verifies DNS TTL behavior.

canary-bot: canary job queued: spike/ephemeral-handshake -> us-west-2/spike-A. expected run: in 1h.

ashley: action items: 1) implement CSR signing + short cert path (ashley) 2) leader/backoff and batch renew (oliver) 3) metrics + dashboard + alerts (kevin) 4) per-tenant kill-switch + ops runbook (sam) 5) security checklist + revocation audit (tess). I'll post bench results and the NAT-flap simulation next update (ts: 3655013020).
